subject.title: Add multi-gateway cron job coordination for HA deployments

question: Should distributed cron ownership be a core feature, a plugin-provided coordination API, or deferred into the broader horizontal-scaling/runtime architecture work?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend choice, config shape, failure semantics, health/CLI visibility, security posture, and core-versus-plugin ownership are maintainer product and architecture decisions.

options.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
options.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, SQLite, or plugin-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

options.title: Fold into broader HA design
options.body: Make this issue a cron-specific requirement of the open horizontal-scaling or distributed-runtime issues and close it only after that design explicitly owns cron scheduling.

options.title: Document external-only operation
options.body: If built-in cron should remain single-Gateway for now, document external scheduler or external lock patterns and mark core HA cron coordination out of scope.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral ownership
recommendation.body: Define a generic cron lease or leader contract before implementation so Redis, etcd, DynamoDB, SQLite, or plugin-backed deployments do not become competing one-off paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current cron scheduler history and already routed this issue as an architecture/product review item.
